title: Kapok: Ancient Kapoks You Can Visit
meta_description: A rainforest giant on buttress roots. Chiapa de Corzo's town square in Mexico was laid out around La Pochota, a ceiba already standing in 1528.
intro: Kapok is a rainforest giant, native to tropical lowland forest where it pushes its crown above the canopy on wide buttress roots. Chiapa de Corzo in Mexico was built around one: when the town was founded on the Grijalva river in 1528, La Pochota already stood where the plaza now sits, and its position was used to lay out the original street grid. A neighbour irritated by its fluff set part of it alight in 1945, and the scorched limb kept growing. Singapore's, at the foot of Mount Faber, has an 11.55 metre girth, among the largest trunks on the city's heritage register. Honolulu's was planted around 1851 by the physician William Hillebrand on his own homestead and is now the oldest tree in the botanical garden later built around it. Lima's holds on in a coastal desert city of grey sea fog.
